title: Staggered introduction mosaic policy engine for safe model swaps
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Implement a configurable policy engine that drives staggered model introductions using 'mosaic' bucketing and phased schedules. Goals: 1) let customers declare multi-step traffic matrices (fractions per cohort, step durations, cooldown windows); 2) enforce guardrails (latency P95, error-rate thresholds, quality regressions) with configurable rollback actions; 3) support shadow probing and A/B cohorts simultaneously; 4) expose observability hooks (per-step telemetry, drift signals) to Console and alerts. Acceptance criteria: policy DSL v0 supports step schedules, cohort selectors, automatic rollback actions, model-variant fallbacks; e2e tests exercising rollback when P95 latency increases >25% or error-rate >1%; Console displays step-level metrics and recommended next-step decisions.
comments: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting notes: scoped initial DSL subset (steps, cohorts, timeouts, rollback thresholds). Decision: MVP will not include probabilistic throttling or entropy-aware routing; focus on deterministic fractional splits and cohort assignments.

2026-02-18: Design review (Lena Park): asked for explicit cooldown semantics between steps to avoid oscillation. Added 'cooldown_seconds' field to DSL proposal. Action: ENG to prototype cooldown enforcement in staging.

2026-02-23: Engineering sync: chose 'mosaic bucketing' approach for cohort assignment so we can shard users deterministically across steps and shadow probes. Trade-off: slight complexity in key derivation vs simpler random sampling. Chosen for reproducible rollouts and easier blame attribution.

2026-02-27: Linked artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/ENG-30988+Mosaic+Policy+Engine, Proto DSL draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1mosaic-dsl-draft, Experimental dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/exp/staggered-intro.

2026-03-01: Prototype results from staging Canary run: 3-step rollout with 3 cohorts. Observed P95 latency bump of 18% at step 2 for model-variant 'v2-quant'. Decision: add an adaptive backoff factor to step-duration recommendation; will not auto-expand to next step until P95 returns within 10% of baseline for two consecutive windows.

2026-03-02: Review comment (PM - Ravi Kumar): ensure config has an explicit 'safety_profile' pointer so we can share reusable threshold sets across customers. Also asked for 'customer_impact' annotation when making policy changes.

2026-03-04: GitHub PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 implementing policy evaluator and mosaic bucketing helper. CI: unit tests for DSL parsing passing; integration tests flaking on simulated latency injection; investigating.

2026-03-05: Security review: preliminary check OK. Set security_review_required to false for MVP but will revisit if we add remote policy import. Next steps: stabilize integration tests, wire metrics to Console, add e2e rollback acceptance tests.

2026-03-05: Note from Assignee (Miguel): blocked briefly by missing metric tag (route_id) in runtime telemetry. Raised ENG-30995 to add the tag; until resolved step-level metrics cannot be correlated to routes in Console.

2026-03-05: QA plan: run three controlled rollouts against synthetic traffic with injected latency and error scenarios, verify rollback triggers, and inspect no-regression on throughput for unaffected routes. Postmortem template prepared: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Rollout+PM+Postmortem+Template.
notes: MVP intentionally omits population-sensitive adaptive splitting and multi-model A/B ranking; those are planned follow-ups (see roadmap). Will iterate on DSL ergonomics after customer trials.
